summary.headline: Sai Silks Q4 FY26 revenue rose 5.1% to ₹419 crore; FY26 revenue up 13.1% to ₹1,654 crore and PAT ₹141 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 5.1% YoY to about ₹419 crore, with PAT of ₹32.65 crore versus ₹13.51 crore a year earlier, helped by a low base. Full-year FY26 revenue rose 13.1% to ₹1,654 crore with same-store sales growth of about 3%, and EBITDA margin expanded to 15.76%. Q4 EBITDA margin was about 14.6%, pressured by advertising timing, employee costs from late-quarter store openings, bonuses and Labour Code impact. Management guided FY27 net addition of about 1 lakh sq ft (at least 20% above FY26), SSSG similar to or slightly above 3%, and EBITDA margin of 17.5-18%.

financial_highlights.change: vs ₹85 crore reported (about +65%); vs ~₹105 crore operational PAT in FY25

segments.name: Varamahalakshmi (VML)
segments.commentary: About 52% of FY26 sales per management; led growth in FY26 and is the highest-margin format, with high-single-digit SSSG in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.

segments.name: Kalamandir
segments.commentary: Expected to lead FY27 expansion in Karnataka (Bangalore focus); FY27 format mix of roughly 60:40 Kalamandir to VML cited.

segments.name: KLM
segments.commentary: Sales declined about 3% in FY26; 9,000 sq ft capacity reduced in one store to improve margin; over 60% of KLM stores are in Telangana, weighing on state SSSG.

segments.name: State mix
segments.commentary: Telangana sales about ₹500 crore in FY26 versus ₹600 crore in FY23; Andhra Pradesh about ₹474 crore versus ₹443 crore; AP grew about 15% and Karnataka about 27%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 net retail addition about 1 lakh sq ft, at least 20% above FY26's ~78,600 sq ft gross addition; may be revised after H1.
FY27 SSSG similar to or slightly better than FY26's ~3%.
FY27 revenue growth expected above FY26's 13.1%; no numeric range given, to be clarified at end of H1.
FY27 EBITDA margin target of at least 17.5% to 18%; full-year EBITDA margin at least +50 bps expected per management.
H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1; April 2026 growth about low single digit positive.
No new borrowings planned in FY27; company is debt-free and expects no borrowing need for the next 2-3 years.
Advertising budget held at about 4% of sales, similar to FY26.
capex_capacity: FY26: 13 new stores and 1 extension added, taking network from 68 to 81 stores across 5 South Indian states; retail area about 785,000 sq ft.
FY26 gross addition about 78,600 sq ft; net addition about 69,000 sq ft after a 9,000 sq ft capacity reduction in Q4.

FY27 pipeline: about 1 lakh sq ft identified and closed; expansion mainly Karnataka (Kalamandir), with some VML stores in Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu; at least one store outside core markets (Maharashtra) expected this year.
Store payback: VML within 8-9 months; maturity to company-average EBITDA margin in 1.5-2 years, longer for Kalamandir.
Inventory rose only ₹34 crore despite about 70,000 sq ft addition; inventory per sq ft down from about ₹11,533 to ₹10,480 since FY24; inventory days about 180 last year.
demand_pricing: Q4 demand softened in late January to February 2026 due to geopolitical and consumption factors; Q4 store openings (2 stores, 25,000 sq ft) came in March 10-15, contributing little revenue.
Tamil Nadu average revenue per sq ft about ₹32,300 for FY26; management expects 5-10% YoY improvement, with potential VML productivity gain of ₹4,000-5,000 per sq ft in Tamil Nadu.
Price increases over the last 6-7 months; average saree budget has moved from about ₹1 lakh to ₹60,000-70,000 per bill.
Gold price hikes expected to divert some spending toward sarees and apparel; management cited Adhik Maas slowdown in early Q1 FY27 until mid-June.
Wedding dates in FY27 expected 5-10% higher than FY26; Dussehra moved to Q3 from Q2 in FY27.
Gross margin protected via vendor discount improvements despite newer lower-margin formats.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 net square feet addition, SSSG and revenue outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Net addition about 1 lakh sq ft (at least 20% above FY26); SSSG similar to or slightly above FY26's ~3%; revenue growth to be firmed up at end of H1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 EBITDA margin fall to about 14.6% despite gross margin above 42%?
qa_highlights.answer: Advertising costs fell about ₹10 crore YoY but some spend landed in Q4; employee costs rose from stores opened Dec 15 to Mar 15, plus bonus (about ₹4 crore, roughly 2 bps) and Labour Code impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 growth slow, and is Valli contributing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied Valli mix as the cause; cited late-January to February consumption slowdown and late-March store openings.

qa_highlights.question: Format-wise sales split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined detailed split but said VML is about 52% of sales and growing as a share.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Telangana and Andhra underperforming?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly KLM, with over 60% of KLM stores in Telangana; VML SSSG in these states is high single digit; new stores are mostly outside Telangana.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Target 17.5-18% for FY27 versus about 16% in FY26, driven by VML mix and productivity gains.

qa_highlights.question: Why not expand faster given the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is focused on maintaining productivity and margins, has closed about 1 lakh sq ft pipeline, and may exceed it after H1.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory days and targets?
qa_highlights.answer: No formal target given; inventory per sq ft reduced to about ₹10,480; FY26 inventory days were about 180.

risks_watch: Q4 EBITDA margin of about 14.6% versus the FY27 17.5-18% target; execution on margin expansion.
Telangana and KLM underperformance and KLM's ~3% decline; plan to revive KLM SSSG not yet quantified.
Tamil Nadu flattening and Q4 sales decline; expected 5-10% productivity improvement is modest.
Depreciation sensitivity to AS 116 lease accounting as new leases are signed.
Entry into a new state (Maharashtra) could raise advertising and store-opening costs.
Inventory days remain high (about 180 last year); no target given.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the structural demand story and the FY27 store pipeline, but cautious and evasive on specific revenue, PAT and inventory numbers, deferring them to the H1 call. Management was defensive when questioned on the promoter and company tax demands and on the Q4 margin slide.
key_quotes: We still delivered strong double-digit revenue growth, significant profitability improvement, sustained margin expansion and also focused on our retail expansion.
One of the top high priority KPIs for us is to maintain the gross margin irrespective of the fact we are coming with the newer formats and lesser gross margin stores.
The challenge is not just opening retail stores and be okay with reduced margins.
The target would be the same. This year, we have reached about 16-point-odd.
